newsitem.title: CHINA: China closes four illegal financial institutions.
newsitem.headline: China closes four illegal financial institutions.

text.p: China has closed four financial institutions that were illegally set up and lent money at higher than official rates, the Xinhua news agency said on Sunday.
Three of the four were in the city of Lanxi, in the eastern province of Zhejiang, which were set up without proper approval between June 1994 and March 1995, it said.

The three paid interest rates on deposits 50 percent higher than official rates and lent money at rates 90 percent higher than official rates. By the end of March this year loans totalled 97 million yuan ($11.7 million), of which 20 percent were outstanding.

From May 20 to early June, there was a run on the banks by depositors when they discovered it would be difficult for the institutions to pay customers because of poor management, the news agency said.
The head of the Lanxi branch of the central bank has been fired for failing to perform proper supervision and those found guilty in the case would be punished under the criminal code.
The fourth institution was in the southwest province of Sichuan, the agency said.
The institution was a mutual assistance fund illegally set up by the trade union of departments directly under the provincial government, it said.
It received funds from grass-roots trade unions and individuals and lent money out in the form of mortgage loans and credit.
By the end of August this year, the fund had debts totalling 500 million yuan. Fund officials have been arrested on suspicion of economic crimes.

Reform of China's financial system has lagged behind reforms in other sectors and many firms cannot obtain capital they need from state banks, which has led to a flourishing non-official credit market.
